U03-ADJ-USE.evidence_note: Strong/weak conditions and agreement. Cook says weak sometimes after possessives; this is not a universal possessive→weak rule.

U03-STRONG.evidence_note: Complete strong pattern, short/long stems, æ/a alternation, disyllabic syncope and optional loss of -u, -e stems, h-loss and consonant simplification.

U03-WEAK.evidence_note: Complete weak pattern. Selected ordinary Gpl -ra; -a/-ena are explicitly admitted alternatives. Comparative Gpl contraction is explained, not a license to invent arbitrary assimilation.

U03-COMPARE.evidence_note: Regular, umlaut and irregular degrees; comparative weak, superlative usually weak. Selected representative series below, not blanket mastery of all examples.

U03-ADVERB.evidence_note: Adverb formation and degree; wīd→wīde, swīð→swīðe very, sōð→sōðlice truly. Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives or adverbs.

U03-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Cardinal/ordinal spellings and complete one/two/three rules; ordinals weak except ōðer.

U03-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: Six agreeing first/second-person possessives; third-person genitives indeclinable. sīn not selected.

U03-DEMONSTRATIVE.evidence_note: Full that/this paradigms. Cook prints short-e ðes, not ðēs; selected double-s variants. Instrumental is reference recognition only.

U03-WRIGHT-USE.evidence_note: Positive/superlative predicate strong; eall and ōðer always strong. Full paradigms confirm agreement; mixed-gender predicate exception remains outside present tasks.

U03-WRIGHT-SYNCOPE.evidence_note: Long-disyllable syncope with retention before consonantal endings; analogical micles/miclum explicitly printed; hāligu and hālgu variants; -erra/-erre may simplify.

U03-WRIGHT-E.evidence_note: Full wilde pattern used by ūre, with its separate fem.Nsg exception in §464.

U03-WRIGHT-GEARU.evidence_note: Complete gearu strong pattern (gearone, gearore, gearora; gearw- before vowel) and weak gearwa/gearwe.

U03-WRIGHT-HEAH.evidence_note: Complete contracted hēah strong pattern and weak hēa, hēan. Selected hēanne/hēarre/hēarra/hēaum; source also gives simpler variants.

U03-WRIGHT-COMPARE.evidence_note: Comparatives weak; irregular series and their variants. Does not individually attest every derived case.

U03-WRIGHT-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Plural ān rare with different distributive sense, not cardinal one with plural count nouns; 4–19 generally uninflected before a noun, with separately conditioned inflection outside this unit.

U03-WRIGHT-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: uncer/incer/ēower explicitly like hālig; ūre like wilde except F.Nsg ūre. ūrre/ūrra may simplify. Combined with §§429/431 yields transparent pattern-derived cells.

U03-WRIGHT-ADVERB.evidence_note: Exact wel/bet/betst and regular -or/-ost pattern; Cook hook spelling selected for bęt/bętst.

U03-THAN.evidence_note: Attested Beowulf469 comparison Sē wæs betere þonne iċ! provides a nominative standard after than with unexpressed repeated copula. Bounded analogous composition, not a claim that all than-constructions take nominative.

U07-C-117.claim: Complete weakI representative indicative/optative/imperative/participle tables, including hīer(e)de plural participle.

U07-C-57-62.claim: Strong/weak adjective models; present -ende like grēne; past participles adjective declension; predicate present usually uninflected and predicate past indeclinable or strong masculine endings.

U07-C-61-62.claim: Participles decline strong and weak adjectivally; predicate inflection is not obligatorily full gender agreement.

U07-C-179.claim: Adjectival participles agree in gender, number and case; predicative participles may be uninflected.

U07-C-187-188.claim: Passive combines past participle with wesan/bēon or weorðan. Only present and preterite are morphologically independent tenses; avoid transferring every Modern English tense/aspect distinction.

U07-C-192-198.claim: Independent commands/wishes and hypothetical uses; gif clauses may have indicative. Later complement, purpose and attraction structures are audited but not automatically assigned.

U07-C-156F.claim: gīemden ðæs dæges explicitly exemplifies genitive government; vocabulary points gīeman to this section.

U07-C-173.claim: Naming verbs may take object accusative and predicate accusative; applicable to attested hātan naming construction.

U07-C-47.claim: Long-stem strong neuters: complete NGDA singular/plural, no nominative/accusative plural ending.

U07-C-89.claim: ǣlc declines like a strong adjective. Quantity explicitly printed; this does not assign the rest of the indefinite-pronoun list.

U07-C-READ124.original_identifier: Reader I Creation, p124 printed lines1–16
U07-C-READ124.claim: Naming hēt...Dæg/Niht/Heofon; tōtwǣman accusative waters+fram dative; tōmiddes, under, bufan with explicit dative. No invented periphrastic hāten clause on this page.

U07-C-READ125.original_identifier: Reader I Creation, p125 printed lines1–15
U07-C-READ125.claim: wæstm wyrcende (note2 explicitly accusative), sǣd berende; bēon tō tācnum gives function tō+dative; actual original forms retained apart from paradigms.

U07-C-READ126.original_identifier: Reader I Creation, p126 printed lines5–14 and notes4–21
U07-C-READ126.claim: Fifth day: Tēon optative3plural; -endu present participles; imperative Weaxað/beōð; independent optative bēon; gemanigfielde plural predicate participle; wæs geworden intransitive resultative close.

U07-C-READ127.original_identifier: Reader I Creation, p127 printed lines2–4,11–17
U07-C-READ127.claim: Authority ofer + explicit accusatives; tō męte dative function and dative beneficiary. These are bounded lexical/prepositional frames, not universal case rules.

U07-F-45-88.claim: Same subjunctive endings -e/-en in each tense, all persons; strong preterite uses indicative-plural vocalism.

U07-F-44-45.claim: Mood is contextual, with exceptions. Preterite subjunctive may be nonpast in unreal/unfulfilled settings; gif does not automatically demand subjunctive.

U07-F-48-50.claim: Two-tense system, ordinary willan volition rather than mechanical future; past/participle constructions and progressive translations require context. Intransitive participial constructions need not be passive.

U07-F-54-56.claim: Disyllabic participial syncope and frequent WestSaxon vowel restoration; present -ende in grēne class; complete strong/weak adjective model support.

U07-F-102.claim: Inherited hātte passive is an exceptional surviving form, not a whole inflectional passive system.

U07-F-107-113.claim: WeakI heavy-stem syncope in inflected participles; short-stem retention; dental and voiceless-contact complications; no universal preterite-minus-e derivation.

U07-F-123.claim: Preterite-present subjunctive lexical forms, variant umlaut, explicitly unattested citation infinitives, missing participles; no formal imperative, subjunctive substituted.

U07-W-429-442.claim: Strong disyllabic and weak adjective models; bunden/holpen map to heavy hālig type, boren/coren/legen to light manig type; participle adjective agreement and predicate uninflection.

U07-W-441-442.claim: Present and past participles decline strong or weak as adjectives; predicate forms often uninflected. Strong participle stem variants have lexical evidence, not arbitrary analogical mutation.

U07-W-477-488.claim: All-person subjunctive endings, first-plural exhortation, present participle ending, preterite subjunctive/participle formation, past-participle ge- history. Historical explanations do not expand learner scope.

U07-F-36-OFER.original_identifier: §36, printed23; Glossary introduction251; Glossary s.v. ofer297
U07-F-36-OFER.claim: Section36 explicitly names ofer among prepositions taking accusative and dative. Glossary297 marks ofer with an obelus; glossary251 defines that mark as the two-case class, with a general direction/location distinction. This proves both governments without deriving them from case-syncretic eorðan. It is not a claim that every sense permits free case substitution or that all prepositions follow an exceptionless motion/rest rule.

features.description: Present and preterite subjunctive each have one singular form for all3persons and one plural form for all3persons. Selected normal endings -e/-en; contracted/anomalous rows explicit. Full672cells+6bēo alternatives.

Use present stem without indicative2/3sg umlaut; use strong preterite plural stem in both subjunctive numbers. Weak past retains its dental stem. Present subjunctive preterite-presents use lexical plural-type/umlauted forms, not strong indicative singular.

Independent present subjunctive expresses wishes/exhortations, including thirdperson Let... and firstplural Letus.... Secondperson imperative and subjunctive are formally/syntactically distinct even where spellings coincide. English let here is not a new lǣtan causative construction.

Open gif clauses can use indicative. A contextually tentative/hypothetical request can use present subjunctive, followed by an imperative or ordinary indicative main clause. Gif itself never licenses an automatic conversion rule.
With explicit unreal/nonpast context and supplied interpretation, preterite subjunctive can refer to nonpast events. No rigid unscaffolded English would template or all counterfactual types assigned.

Keep learned mæg capability, mōt permission, wille/wolde volition distinct from inflectional subjunctive wishes. A past spelling does not mechanically mean English would/might; willan is not automatically future. Preserve bounded earlier cunnan/ðurfan/durran/sculan senses.

Complete present/past formation pairs for12selected lemmas; other roster citations remain audit-only. Source libbendu/flēogendu/swimmendu receive recognition with full mapped -ende pattern; participial accompaniment cweðende remains locally supplied syntax.
Full48NGDA strong/weak cells per selected model; attributive participles follow adjective choice and agreement. Distinguish predicate participles, which may be uninflected or strong-masculine-like.

For assigned accusative-object verbs, present or preterite wesan/bēon or weorðan + past participle expresses passive. Finite auxiliary agrees with the nominative subject. Agent omitted in productive tasks; no new fram-agent rule needed. Wesan often presents state/result and weorðan event, but not an absolute contrast or one-to-one English tense mapping.
Wæs geworden in Creation is become/come-to-pass resultative close, not a transitive passive. Perfects/progressives/absolutes remain outside independent production.

Active hātan naming can take object accusative + name/predicate accusative. Ordinary periphrastic passive (ge)hāten derives from the checked participle+auxiliary rule; inherited hātte remains audit-only.
Promote eall strong NGDA and introduce image-checked longǣlc strong NGDA. Complete models do not teach unrelated indefinite pronouns, partitives, adverbial quantifier idioms or weak paradigms.
Rule over the genitive object.

features.description: Complete twelve-cell indicative systems of wyrcean, gīeman, rīcsian, gemanigfieldan and tōtwǣman, preserving their individually taught lexical scope.
Complete second-singular and second-plural imperative of tōtwǣman; accusative separated thing and fram+dative landmark.

Spatial ofer permits the source-attested accusative/dative constructions. Fulk§36 explicitly verifies both governments; exact eorðan is syncretic, so its surface alone cannot prove either case. Authority ofer+accusative is separately taught. No unrestricted case interchange or exceptionless motion/rest rule is assigned.
A separate dative beneficiary can accompany a copular clause with tō+dative assigned function, as ēow tō męte; the beneficiary is not a possessive adjective.

Nū now, swā so, ðus thus, ēac also and swilce likewise are invariant adverbs; efne behold introduces a statement as an interjection. Nū is may precede its nominal subject in the given presentational frame. The conjunction swilce as if is unassigned.
The learned second-person imperative or new present subjunctive of the auxiliary combines with the selected past participle to command or wish a passive situation. The participle is nonfinite.
Previously taught direct quotation now includes the independently taught subjunctive wish/exhortation and basic conditional. Quoted pronouns belong to the quoted speaker’s setting.
In verbal predicates a past participle may be uninflected or take strong-masculine-like endings: neuter plural dēor bunden/bundene are both licensed. Attributive agreement remains a different target.
Selected full-vowel participial agreement models coexist with listed syncope variants; weak dental principal parts are lexical and cannot uniformly be recovered as past-minus-e.
Supply tēon ... forð / tugon forð as bring forth. The finite morphology may be taught, but draw/pull does not automatically supply this lexical sense.
Supply cucu on līfe as alive, with exact irregular cucu. It is not the ordinary locative on frame alone.
Supply ðe ðā wæteru tugon forð on hiera hīwum, which the waters brought forth in their forms/kinds. ðe is accusative object and waters nominative subject.
Supply on hiera hīwum and æfter hiera cynne as in their forms/kinds and according to their kind; no general new prepositional production.
Supply God geseah ðā ðæt hit gōd wæs as God then saw that it was good. Content conjunction, clause boundary and source verb-final order remain supplied.
Supply ðus cweðende as saying thus, accompanying God’s blessing. The participial form is productive, but this accompanying-action construction is not independently assigned.
Supply the continuation And blētsode hīe: God remains the subject and hīe is the accusative plural object; the exact plain blētsian is distinct from productive geblētsian.

mendu cynn cucu on līfe, and flēogendu cynn ofer eorðan
under ðǣre heofonan fæstnesse.” And God gescēop ðā ðā
miclan hwalas, and eall libbendu fisccynn and styriend-
licu, ðe ðā wæteru tugon forð on hiera hīwum, and
eall flēogendu cynn æfter hiera cynne; God geseah ðā ðæt

readings.learner_text: God cwæð ēac swilce, “Tēon nū ðā wæteru forð swimmendu cynn cucu on līfe, and flēogendu cynn ofer eorðan under ðǣre heofonan fæstnesse.” And God gescēop ðā ðā miclan hwalas, and eall libbendu fisccynn and styriendlicu, ðe ðā wæteru tugon forð on hiera hīwum, and eall flēogendu cynn æfter hiera cynne; God geseah ðā ðæt hit gōd wæs. And blētsode hīe, ðus cweðende, “Weaxað, and bēoð gemanigfielde, and gefyllað ðǣre sǣ wæteru, and ðā fuglas bēon gemanigfielde ofer eorðan.” And ðā wæs geworden ǣfen and męrgen se fīfta dæg.
change_notes: No Old English word, spelling, quantity mark, grammatical ending, or punctuation is changed.
Printed prose line wrapping is removed; the two purely line-end hyphens swim-/mendu and styriend-/licu are removed when joining their words.
Superscript original note cues4–21 are detached from the running text and preserved in the separate note inventory.
Quotation marks are represented by modern Unicode curved double quotation marks; source quotation boundaries are retained.
The hooked e in męrgen is retained; this is not silently normalized to morgen.

supports.support: Bring forth / brought forth. Tēon is a present third-plural subjunctive with ðā wæteru as its subject; tugon is past third-plural indicative. The bring-forth sense and split phrase are supplied; prior tēon draw/pull alone does not cover them.
supports.scope: Local supplied context; grammatical forms expressly promoted elsewhere retain their new status.

supports.source_span: swimmendu cynn cucu on līfe; flēogendu cynn
supports.support: Swimming kinds, alive/living; flying kinds. The -u participles and cucu are neuter accusative plural with cynn, the things to be brought forth. Cook calls cucu irregular. Supply actual -u forms and the alive expression; do not use the source to infer that every -ende participle mechanically loses e before -u.
supports.scope: Local supplied context; grammatical forms expressly promoted elsewhere retain their new status.

supports.source_span: ofer eorðan; under ðǣre heofonan fæstnesse
supports.support: Over the earth; under the firmament of heaven. Heofonan is genitive singular of source weak feminine heofone; fæstnesse is dative after under. Ðǣre is formally feminine genitive or dative singular: agreement with genitive heofonan or dative fæstnesse is compatible with the spelling, so do not uniquely grade its case. Eorðan alone is likewise accusative/dative syncretic after spatial ofer; no uniquely graded case diagnosis is warranted.
supports.scope: Local supplied context; grammatical forms expressly promoted elsewhere retain their new status.

supports.source_span: ðā ðā miclan hwalas; eall libbendu fisccynn and styriendlicu
supports.support: The first ðā is then; the second is the article with great whales. Fisccynn is neuter accusative plural fish-kinds; libbendu and styriendlicu describe it. Preserve the source styriendlicu -u as a supplied variant, distinct from Unit3 selected styriendlic. Do not silently create a second noun meaning after and.
supports.scope: Local supplied context; grammatical forms expressly promoted elsewhere retain their new status.

supports.source_span: ðe ðā wæteru tugon forð on hiera hīwum
supports.support: Which the waters brought forth according to their forms/kinds. Relative ðe is the object (original note12); ðā wæteru is the subject (note13). Supply the whole relative construction and on hiera hīwum; hīw is neuter, here dative plural.
supports.scope: Local supplied context; grammatical forms expressly promoted elsewhere retain their new status.

supports.support: According to their kind; æfter governs dative cynne here. Supply the phrase and the preposition’s classificatory sense.
supports.scope: Local supplied context; grammatical forms expressly promoted elsewhere retain their new status.

supports.source_span: God geseah ðā ðæt hit gōd wæs
supports.support: God then saw that it was good. Supply the content clause introduced by ðæt, its verb-final order, and the nonhuman situation reference of hit; familiar indicative forms do not establish general content-clause syntax.
supports.scope: Local supplied context; grammatical forms expressly promoted elsewhere retain their new status.

supports.support: And [God] blessed them, saying thus. The subject God continues from the preceding clause. Blētsode is the supplied past3sg of plain blētsian, distinct from earlier geblētsian. Cweðende refers to the same subject; support this attendant participle construction unless expressly taught.
supports.scope: Local supplied context; grammatical forms expressly promoted elsewhere retain their new status.

supports.source_span: Weaxað … bēoð … gefyllað; ðā fuglas bēon gemanigfielde
supports.support: First the created beings are addressed by plural imperatives. The birds are then named in a third-person plural subjunctive wish. Gemanigfielde is the source nominative plural past participle, retained in the passive. Gefyllað means fill here, a new sense beyond finish/accomplish. Ðǣre sǣ wæteru means waters of the sea: sǣ is source feminine genitive singular, and ðǣre agrees with it; it is not the earlier selected masculine genitive sǣs.
supports.scope: Local supplied context; grammatical forms expressly promoted elsewhere retain their new status.

supports.source_span: And ðā wæs geworden ǣfen and męrgen se fīfta dæg
supports.support: And then evening and morning had come to be, the fifth day. Supply the resultative closing formula with intransitive geweorðan; it is not a transitive passive. Preserve source męrgen. Do not demand an unsupported general agreement rule or a unique clause analysis from this formula.

Cook61: present participles in the predicate as nominative/accusative are generally uninflected. Cook62: predicate past participles are generally indeclinable or take strong masculine endings. Cook179 allows uninflected predicate participles. Thus neuterplural dēor bunden is acceptable; dēor bundene is also licensed in verbal passive usage. Do not judge them by an obligatory attributive neuter-u rule.

Heavy-stem disyllabic participles can lose the unstressed vowel before vowel-initial inflections: bundenes→bundnes, bundenum→bundnum; hīeredes→hīerdes, hīeredum→hīerdum, hīerede→hīerde. Full vowels are often restored in West Saxon. Keep the full stem before -ne/-re/-ra; doubled n in bundenne is ordinary. Short-root fręmed/nęred and lufod retain their vowel in the selected model. Rare -u cells above are transparently paradigm-derived.

Weak participles are lexical principal parts, not a universal past-minus-e shortcut: hīerde→hīered, fręmede→fręmed, lufode→lufod, sealde→seald, worhte→worht, sętte→sętt, sęnde→sęnd, lǣdde→lǣd. Before inflection, syncope can bring a dental into contact with a voiceless stem and cause -t-, as Fulk113 scierped→scierpte. These audit examples do not newly assign unlisted verbs.

A past participle of an intransitive verb need not be passive. Source wæs geworden is a become/come-to-pass resultative closure, not a transitive passive. Auxiliary tense does not force one Modern English tense/aspect translation.
